root_idea.summary: The root centers on holding back or restraining, especially restraining oneself from impatience; it also has distinct branches involving upper edges and hard or collected stone.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from self-restraint and confinement to things held together, heaped, or made firm, while a separate branch denotes the upper or edge portions of things and stones or stony ground.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Form III reciprocal or competitive construction.
Feminine plural active-participle inflection of صَابِر.

senses.definition: To restrain oneself from impatience and endure hardship with patience; to remain steadfast.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for enduring affliction, resisting desire, remaining firm in obedience, and withholding complaint. It may be intransitive, or occur with the self understood or with عَلَى or عَنْ.

senses.definition: To wait patiently for an appointed outcome or judgment.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic use of patient endurance with an expected ruling or outcome, as in صَبْرٌ لِحُكْمٍ; it is more than mere passive delay.

senses.definition: In the exclamatory construction ما أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ: to be astonishingly bold or heedless in exposing oneself to the Fire.
senses.usage_conditions: This Quranic construction presents the people addressed as extraordinarily bold to undertake the deeds leading to the Fire, rather than simply praising their patience.

senses.definition: To vie with one another in patience or endurance; to mutually hold firm in trial.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَصَابِرُوا, the construction conveys active competition or mutual outlasting in patience, conventionally presented as a stronger progression than merely enduring oneself.

senses.definition: To labor to maintain patience; to persevere steadfastly.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction اِصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَادَتِهِ emphasizes sustained, effortful perseverance in worship or another demanding course.

senses.definition: One who is patient, enduring, and steadfast.
senses.usage_conditions: An active-participial epithet for a person who restrains the self and remains firm through affliction, obedience, struggle, or deprivation; the Quran applies the form to masculine and feminine groups as well as individuals.

senses.definition: Patience, endurance, or self-restraint from impatience.
senses.usage_conditions: A general noun for maintaining composure and withholding oneself from complaint or impulsive response in hardship, duty, or trial.

senses.definition: Marked by very great or persistent patience; intensely steadfast.
senses.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective for someone whose patience involves unusual constancy, effort, or struggle rather than a merely occasional act of endurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confine, detain, retain, restrain, or withhold a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use, including restraint from or withholding something with عَنْهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Boldness or daring in enduring or attempting something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical extension of endurance toward courageous or audacious undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or confine a living being until death; a being so held for killing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes deliberate confinement for slaughter or execution, whether by bonds or by setting the victim up to be shot or otherwise killed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confine or constrain someone until an oath is sworn; an oath imposed under such custody.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated oath may itself be called مَصْبُورَةٌ by a tropical extension, while the person is the one literally confined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave or cling to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct intransitive or relational use, synonymous with remaining attached to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become responsible or act as surety for someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun صَبِيرٌ denotes the person who undertakes the liability or guarantee.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To heap or gather a thing into a compact mass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to gathering grain or goods together without measuring or weighing; a related passive description is being collected into such a mass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge, command, require, or make someone patient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May involve promising a reward, attributing patience to someone, or enjoining endurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To embalm a dead body with the substance called صَبِر.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported with explicitly limited authority in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ballast a ship; ballast placed in the bottom of a ship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the weight used to stabilize a vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To retaliate by killing, wounding, or otherwise answering an injury in kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A legal or combative use of the derived forms, distinct from ordinary patience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hard or intense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a thing that has become firm or severe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stony tract or lava field of hard, dark, worn stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the terrain called حَرَّةٌ and related hard, smooth, or difficult ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity, severe war, or inescapably distressing situation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiom for falling into a grave and perplexing predicament.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain or particular mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also be used for a prominent elevated mass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of milk, to become very sour and incline toward bitterness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized sensory use connected with the bitterness of صَبِر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thin, round cake of bread used beneath or with food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be spread beneath food or used at a wedding feast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stopper or plug for a bottle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Synonymous with سَدَادٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be patient or endure one with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a group acting mutually in patience or endurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To league together and aid one another against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with عَلَى, distinct from mutual endurance itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a vapor, to become dense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fasting as an act of self-restraint from food, drink, and sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional designation for fasting, presented as a type of restraint rather than as the general noun's primary meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper part, side, edge, or thickness of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the upper edges or sides of vessels and graves, and figuratively for taking something altogether.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land containing pebbles but not rugged ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A terrain term related to stony ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal lexical item, distinct from صَبْرٌ meaning patience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aloe or the expressed juice of a bitter medicinal plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the dried medicinal extract and its uninflected plant name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Myrrh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported by Freytag, while the lexical discussion notes that independent authority for this identification is lacking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Urine and dung of camels or other beasts compacted together in a watering place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized concrete noun for a compacted accumulation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular bird with a red body and dark head, wings, and tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bird is also reported under closely related diminutive or variant forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity of grain or another commodity collected and heaped without measuring or weighing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes reaped or threshed grain gathered in the place where it is processed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wheat sifted with a net-like implement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough or rugged stones collected together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A pluralized or collective material use of the same lexical item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The intensely acid fruit of a tree, used medicinally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The صِبَارٌ spelling is reported as possibly an error for صُبَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone, a piece of stone, a mass of stones, or a piece of iron.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural and variant forms can refer collectively to stones or other hard pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chief, director, or manager of a people's affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explained as one who patiently manages affairs for and with a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A solitary man without offspring or a brother.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported by Golius but explicitly suspected in the source of being an error for صُنْبُورٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A white or dense cloud, especially one stationary or layered above another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical descriptions include clouds slow to move, remaining stationary, or arranged like steps.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hill consisting of stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported, weakly attested terrain sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The intense cold of winter, or the middle of winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote either the severity of winter's cold or its central period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rugged, elevated, hard ground without herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A terrain term for barren ground rising above adjacent land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long-suffering or forbearing, especially as an epithet of God who does not hasten to avenge disobedience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized theological application of the patience epithet, emphasizing deferred vengeance and clemency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most patient; more enduring than another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective used for unusually great endurance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sheep, goats, or camels that return morning and evening to their owners.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural noun reported as having no established singular.

cautions: The QAC Form I grouping includes the exclamatory occurrence ما أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ; it is represented separately from ordinary patience because its Quranic interpretation is boldness or heedlessness.
Several rare classical branches are explicitly qualified in the evidence, especially the reported myrrh sense, the solitary-man sense, and the uncertain collected-flesh report.
